items.claim: In a Claude Code skill's frontmatter, the description field is what Claude reads to decide when to load the skill, and disable-model-invocation: true stops Claude from loading it on its own, so it only runs when you invoke it.
items.why_it_matters: If you write descriptions as triggers and lock skills with side effects, agents stop firing deploy or merge workflows by surprise.
items.try_this: Add disable-model-invocation: true to any of your skills that merges, deploys or sends messages.

verification.method: Claude Code skills docs frontmatter table confirms both fields and their behavior

items.excerpt: Claude can't invoke the skill on its own.

items.claim: T3 Code nightly builds include a Working section that holds threads whose background work the agent is waiting on, and threads settle once their PR is merged.
items.why_it_matters: This keeps finished or waiting agent threads out of your active inbox when many agents run at once.

verification.method: Oct 25 nightly notes mention Working and thread settling after a merge; Theo's 'every 6 hours' cadence claim not confirmed

items.claim: Theo's full-send skill has an agent take a change all the way to a merged PR: prove it works, review it, file the PR, watch CI and review bots, then merge. full-stop does the same but stops before merging.
items.why_it_matters: It shows a concrete merge gate and proof step for autonomous agents. full-stop is the safer version if you want a human to merge.
items.try_this: Start with a full-stop style flow, where the agent prepares a PR and a person merges it, before allowing any agent to merge.

verification.method: tstack README describes full-send and full-stop as stated; skill not executed

items.excerpt: Same as full-send, but stops when the PR is ready for you to merge.

items.claim: tstack includes cross-model review skills. sol-loop has a GPT Sol model review a change in a loop until both agents agree, and council gets reviews from three models from different providers until they agree.
items.why_it_matters: Pairing an authoring model with a reviewer from another vendor is a cheap way to catch mistakes that one model misses.
items.try_this: On one non-critical PR, ask a model from a different vendor to review your main agent's diff and compare what each one finds.

verification.method: README lists sol-loop and council as described; the 3 to 5 round budget is only in the video

items.claim: Theo has published tstack, an MIT-licensed GitHub repo of his daily agent skills for Claude Code and Codex. It includes full-send, full-stop, sol-loop, council, takeover, babysit-pr, modernize, file-pr and leaving-pr-comments.
items.why_it_matters: You can read how a heavy agent user structures reusable skills for PR work and borrow the parts that fit your own workflow.
items.try_this: Read the full-stop skill file in the tstack repo and compare its steps with your own PR checklist before adopting anything.

verification.method: Repo fetched: exists, MIT license, README lists the named skills; no sandbox run
verification.audit_note: Repo t3dotgg/tstack: MIT license, 'agent skills I use every day', for Claude Code and Codex; all nine skills listed.

items.excerpt: The agent skills I use every day, cleaned up so anyone can use them.

items.claim: T3 Code is an open-source control surface for coding agents, with desktop, web and mobile apps. It drives Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other harnesses on your own machine and supports remote access.
items.why_it_matters: One interface for several agent harnesses across machines can make it easier to manage parallel agent threads.
items.try_this: Read the T3 Code README and its remote-access doc to see whether it fits your setup before installing anything.

verification.method: T3 Code GitHub README confirms the harness list and the mobile/remote apps; not run

items.claim: Simon Willison released Seam Cutter, a browser tool that cuts an image horizontally or vertically and slides the two halves together, removing a strip from the middle, for example to redact a prompt from a stitched transcript screenshot.
items.why_it_matters: It is a quick way to remove irrelevant or sensitive prompt text from long agent-transcript screenshots before you share them.
items.try_this: Open the Seam Cutter page in your browser and remove one section from a long screenshot of an agent transcript.

verification.method: Tool page fetched: exists and accepts an image for a seam cut; behavior taken from the blog post, not tested
verification.audit_note: Tool page lacks details; directory entry and Simon's 25 Oct blog post confirm the cut, slide and transcript-redaction example.

items.excerpt: it lets you create a horizontal or vertical cut across an image, then slide the two sides relative to each other.

items.claim: Theo says T3 Code Nightly added Orchestrator v2, where a main agent thread hands work to subagents running in other harnesses and models, each in its own worktree, which report back.
items.why_it_matters: If shipped, it would allow mixed-vendor subagent review inside one tool, but this is not confirmed yet.

verification.method: Release notes and README checked; no mention of Orchestrator v2 or cross-harness subagents
